In ‘Steps,’ Stephanie Hsu got to be as grotesque as she wanted

She talks voice acting in the "Cinderella" reimagining, finding belonging, and seeing a blended family in a fairy tale story

Margot, voiced by Stephanie Hsu, gets turned into a frog in Netflix's "Steps."

Netflix Animation Studios

(opens in new tab)(opens in new tab)(opens in new tab)

Words by Rasha Goel

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 1:40
Instaread

What happens when Cinderella’s so-called “evil” stepsisters finally get to tell their side of the story? Netflix’s upcoming animated adventure Steps turns the beloved fairy tale upside down, putting the spotlight on the characters who have traditionally been cast as the villains. Featuring the voices of Ali Wong, Stephanie Hsu, Amanda Seyfried, Nikki Glaser and Bette Midler, the film follows sisters Lilith (Wong) and Margot (Hsu), and their stepsister Cinderella (Seyfried), as a stolen magic wand, a hijacked royal ball, and an unexpected turn of events send their kingdom into chaos. But beneath the humor, magic, and action is a story about sisterhood, identity, belonging, and challenging the labels others place on us. 

JoySauce talked to Hsu about bringing this reimagined character to life, finding the heart and personality behind an animated role, and why stories that challenge our perceptions of who is good and who is bad are more important than ever. Our chat also included how a mixed-race family adds another layer to the story, as Asian American talent is highlighted in the film. Steps is now streaming on Netflix.

Published on November 23, 2026

Words by Rasha Goel
